title: C13 gate policy v0 (registry artifact — WHETHER WE SHIP IT)
description: The publish-gate policy, served verbatim by storage's registry at GET /policies/{policy_id}. A SEPARATE ARTIFACT FROM THE RECIPE, with a separate id, a separate schema and a separate lifecycle — this is the whole reason C13 has two shapes rather than one. `recipe_id` is hashed into continuum's amplify and train stage keys; `policy_id` is recorded in the gate report and MUST NEVER enter a stage key. Keeping thresholds inside the recipe was a real trap, not a tidiness point: a threshold edit would fork `recipe_id`, invalidate the amplify and train caches, re-run a night of GPU time, and imply the trained artifact had changed when only our willingness to publish it did. Re-deciding what is good enough to ship must never re-train anything. Thresholds ratified by the cofounders 2026-07-24 from measured distributions. Like the recipe schema, additional properties are ALLOWED: this artifact carries per-threshold rationale prose (`traps_note`, `min_probes_note`, `heldout.note`) that records why a number moved, and it belongs in the artifact rather than beside it.

policy_id.description: The policy's identity AND its filename stem (`<policies_dir>/<policy_id>.json`). Path-safe by pattern because it resolves to a file. Versioned independently of any recipe: gate-policy-v1.1 supersedes the gate/publish block formerly inside recipes/consolidation-v1.0.json, and no recipe_id moved when it did.

ratified.description: Optional provenance prose: who ratified these numbers, when, and from which measurement.

supersedes.description: Optional provenance prose: what this policy replaced.

note.description: Optional prose. The load-bearing sentence lives here in v1.1: policy_id must never enter a cycle stage key.

gate.description: What an adapter must clear to be publishable. Every previous value blocked ~everything, including the validated recipe's own output — these are measured, not aspirational.

new_day_recall_min.description: Minimum recall on the night's own new-day probes — did consolidation learn today at all.

traps_pass_min.description: Minimum deny-then-correct trap pass rate — the collapse detector.

heldout.description: The contamination check, run against the run's OWN base control rather than a fixed ceiling: a constant asks 'did this run score above 0.05', which conflates a leak with a base model that happens to know things, and breaks entirely the day the base model changes.

alpha.description: One-sided exact-test significance level vs the run's own base control.

backstop.description: Absolute ceiling, for a base model that is itself contaminated — the case where the differential test would see nothing.

probes.description: How many heldout probes the eval must run.

min_probes.description: Floor on total probes before a gate verdict means anything. A floor the harness cannot supply is unpassable by construction — 148 is measured against what it actually supplies (60 + 60 + 28).

decay_retention_min.description: Minimum retention of prior nights' material — the forgetting check.

consecutive_fail_freeze.description: How many consecutive gate failures freeze the user's cycle. A freeze leaves `last_trained_t` exactly where it was, so the next window is a strict superset.

snapshot_retention.description: How many published adapter snapshots to keep for rollback. NOT a data-retention policy — user content is keep-everything; this is about adapter artifacts.

unwired_checks.description: Checks named in the policy but not yet executed by the harness. Listed in the artifact ON PURPOSE: a threshold nobody runs is worse than no threshold, and writing them down here is what keeps that visible instead of implied.
